paper.title: Content-Level Selective Offloading in Heterogeneous Networks: Multi-armed Bandit Optimization and Regret Bounds

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial MAB with switching cost (CMABSC) for optimal caching
unmapped: Feasible arm combinations are sets of files satisfying a knapsack (cache capacity M, file sizes S_f) constraint
Reward of a set is U*sum S_f theta_f; switching cost w*sum of sizes of newly added files
Regret measured against alpha*beta times optimum using an (alpha,beta)-approximation oracle (solver succeeds w.p. beta)
Regret = sampling regret + w * switching regret
settings.definition_quote: Since the instantaneous demand for each file is iid over time with an unknown mean value, and only the demands associated to $\mathcal{M}^t_\pi$ are observed, (\ref{CAeq:opt_PG}) is a CMABSC problem.

bound.expression: log(T)*(6/gl**2*(w + Delta_u/(2*(M_u - M_l))) + w*gamma_sc/2)*2*K*(M_u - M_l) + sqrt(T)*(w*M_u + w*(M_u - M_l)*(1 - 2*beta_s) + K*Delta_u*gamma_sc) + (pi**2/3 + 4.12*gamma_sc + 1)*K*Delta_u + w*C_const

symbols.gl: g^{-1}(Delta_l), inverse of the linear reward-perturbation function evaluated at Delta_l
symbols.Delta_u: alpha*r_opt minus the minimum reward of a bad arm combination
symbols.M_u: maximum switching cost between two arm combinations
symbols.M_l: maximum switching cost between two good arm combinations
symbols.C_const: constant independent of t defined in the appendix

conditions: access to an (alpha,beta)-solver for the single-period problem
regret is w.r.t. alpha*beta*r_opt plus w times switching regret

results.notes: F (number of files) mapped to K, t to T. Regret defined via expected rewards (sampling regret) plus weighted expected switching cost; recorded as pseudo_regret. Comparator is the alpha-beta approximate optimal set.

symbols.Delta_u: alpha*r_opt minus the minimum reward of a bad arm combination
symbols.M_u: maximum switching cost between two arm combinations

conditions: alpha = beta = 1: solver returns the unique optimal solution
